why_next: This packet's decision-relevant yield is a negative about the question the mandate asked, and it is a negative about the corpus, not about SPIDER. No source in the five-artifact corpus publishes a goal-to-artifact binding error rate, so the external bar C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE was supposed to inherit does not exist; the only open-natural-language system (arXiv:2604.09718) is behind a mandatory unquantified human review gate, reports schema validity rather than binding error, and declares its own evaluation non-replicable. Two things are therefore unresolvable from what has now been read, and both are cheap to resolve. (a) The single unmeasured quantity that would actually decide 'externally preempted' versus 'unoccupied' is the amendment rate of arXiv:2604.09718's mandatory review gate - the paper publishes none, so it may plausibly be published in a follow-up, docs site or engineering write-up, or it may not exist anywhere. (b) One of the five mandated targets, COVENANT, was never located, so recall over the mandate's own target list is unmeasured and the negative inherits that gap. Running the same shaped search again without repairing the three design defects the audit exposed (identity-before-scoring, a control that can fail, accounting conventions and denominators) would produce another non-discriminating null: NC-FABRICATED-BINDING-CLAIMS searched for three literal phrases no paper would contain and detected nothing while a mandated target was being substituted underneath it. A materially different question is therefore available and is the one proposed: decompose the under-specified 'binding error rate' construct into four separately reportable quantities and search the whole external surface, not just the five artifacts the mandate happened to name. Beneficiaries are graph (C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE now has no external comparator and must set its own bar), product (the composite MV6 baseline cannot be a bar, and the break-even conventions are now known), and frontier (the F3 datum makes 'witnessed-determinism predicts compilability' a falsifiable claim with a published counterexample already in hand). DETERMINISM DOES NOT IMPLY COMPILABILITY - the most decision-relevant new datum for C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE and C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY. arXiv:2607.04542's determinism census reports F1 100.0%, F2 77.5% (sub-spans classify 100.0 / priority 92.5 / summarize 17.5 / tool 100.0), F3 100.0%, F4 100.0%, pooled 560/560 = 87.1% (audit recomputation from family rows = 0.8714, confirming the published figure), yet F3 is REFUSED at all three rungs, and F4's holdout passes at exactly its declared 90.0% threshold (36/40). Under a deliberately loose guard (alpha=0.1) the same paper reports 48.9% silent wrongness (133/272) and concludes that 'Calibration and reference fidelity, not model capability, decide whether cheap stays correct'. The census covers FOUR families (F1-F4), not the '6 task families' framing in result.json validity_notes[3]; F5 exists separately in Table 2 as a judged family (FAIL 17/40 = 42.5% against an 800 per-mille threshold).

B-MV6-NO-MEMORY-EXECUTOR is a CROSS-SYSTEM COMPOSITE, not one system, and its latency endpoint understates its own source by ~3,610x. Compilation cost comes from arXiv:2604.09718, witnessed-determinism and the latency ladder from arXiv:2607.04542, refusal evidence from arXiv:2608.02680, schema compression from arXiv:2605.04107, latency and TCO from arXiv:2604.05150; no consulted system instantiates all of it. The 18.2 microsecond endpoint is arXiv:2607.04542's in-process Node RESIDENT dispatch floor, measured 'on a trivial artifact rather than model inference', while the same paper's Table 2 measures 65.7 ms per compiled answer (F1 triage, F2 classify, F4 routing) - ratio 3,609.9. Its 'token cost 0 on repeats' endpoint is TSCG's (a schema compiler with no per-task execution) plus Compiled AI's BFCL-specific zero runtime tokens. Three lanes were told to beat this bar; the bar is optimistic and has no single owner.

ACCOUNTING CONVENTIONS, now recovered, without which no break-even is computable. arXiv:2607.04542: 6.4x is a TOTAL-STREAM-SPEND ratio (17,692/2,775 = 6.375) while the abstract's '59 to 2 micro-dollars per item' is a PER-ITEM ratio (59.0/2.3 = 25.65x, steady state 2.3); the same paper elsewhere asserts 'three orders of magnitude', inconsistent with both of its own figures. arXiv:2604.05150: 40x TCO is computed at 1M transactions/month with an identical fixed 500 USD/month infrastructure line present in every row, so ~90% of the compiled arm's 555 USD is fixed infra and the inference-only ratio is 21,500/55 = 390.9x; break-even recomputes to n* = 9,600/552 = 17.39; token ratio 552,000/9,600 = 57.5x at 1,000 transactions, 805,000/9,600 = 83.85x against AutoGen; latency 2,004/4.5 = 445.3x.
